Data Sources The principal source of information for the tables in International Debt Report 2026 is the International Debt Statistics database, which is based on reports to the World Bank through the World Bank’s Debtor Reporting System (DRS) from member countries that have received either International Bank for Reconstruction and Development loans or International Development Association credits. The DRS has its origin in the World Bank’s need to monitor and assess the financial position of its borrowers. Since 1951, borrowers have been required to provide statistics on their public external debt and private sector debt that benefit from a public guarantee. Reporting countries submit reports on the annual status, transactions, and terms of the long-term external debt of public agencies and that of private ones guaranteed by a public agency in the debtor country. The DRS maintains these records on a loan-by-loan basis. In 1973, coverage of the DRS was expanded to include private sector nonguaranteed borrowing; however, for this category of debt, data are provided by borrowers in aggregate rather than loan by loan.

Progress in Debt Transparency, 2020–25 Debt transparency is at the center of the World Bank Group’s engagement with its borrowers and partners. The policy commitment of the International Development Association (IDA) is to support debt sustainability and debt transparency through technical assistance, knowledge, and financing engagements. The Sustainable Development Finance Policy (SDFP), which became effective in July 2020, requires IDA-eligible borrowers at moderate or elevated risk of debt distress to take concrete policy performance actions (PPAs) to enhance debt transparency, strengthen debt management, and promote fiscal sustainability.1 These PPAs have been instrumental in incentivizing countries to embrace sustainable development financing, embed debt transparency reforms into national policy frameworks, and institutionalize transparent disclosure of public debt data.

In its first year in operation, fiscal year (FY) 2021, 55 IDA countries committed to 130 PPAs. By FY2026, these numbers had risen to 65 IDA countries implementing 159 PPAs, of which 55 percent focused on debt transparency and debt management. During the initial years of implementation, PPAs related to debt transparency focused on foundational measures aimed at disclosure of timely and comprehensive debt bulletins. They also focus on strengthening institutional structures for debt management, including the creation of dedicated debt offices, strong legal and governance frameworks, and enhanced procedures for managing sovereign guarantees, on-lending, and borrowing by SOEs.
